name: Technocracy movement
summary: The technocracy movement, centred on Howard Scott's Technocracy Inc. in the 1930s and 40s, held that the Price System of money, wages and profit was collapsing under the impact of machine energy and had to be replaced by a continental Technate run by technically trained functional hierarchies. Goods were to be distributed in equal energy certificates with no money, a four-hour day and early retirement, and politics, elections and democratic theory were rejected as unscientific. In 1940 it also campaigned for total conscription and continental defence.
scope: The North American movement of Technocracy Inc. and its predecessor the Technical Alliance (Howard Scott, 1919 onward; Introduction to Technocracy, the Technocracy Study Course, Technocracy in Plain Terms, Technocracy magazine, Scott's later talks). It is not the general doctrine of rule by experts (Saint-Simon, Veblen, modern technocratic governments), which has its own entry, and not the Soviet engineers' movement or Veblen's Soviet of Technicians. Positions on war and defence are those of the 1940-41 programme; the movement's own claim to be science, not ideology, is recorded as its stated method.
